clue.text: Bland statement removing first freedom

indicators.note: removing first tells us to drop the opening letter of the bland-statement word

parts.note: a platitude is a trite, bland remark

explanation.surface: A dull remark takes away someone's most important liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing first' strips the P from PLATITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is scope or leeway to act as one wishes, a synonym for freedom.

clue.text: Lag to the rear in makeshift boat?

parts.note: a lag is a convict, and a lifer is one serving a life sentence
aft is the nautical word for towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone lagging behind at the back of an improvised vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' is the old slang for a convict, here a long-term prisoner. The grid prints P for F; the wordplay builds the real word.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable survival craft is an emergency vessel, which the question mark lets stand as a makeshift boat.

clue.text: Artisan transformed into imperial figure

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the craftsman word are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A craftsman is turned into royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges ARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the empress of Russia, a figure of imperial rank.

clue.text: Family, note, including wife

indicators.note: including means the note's letters hold the wife's letters within them

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
rib is slang for a wife, from Eve being made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A family message that mentions the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' signals the container. Wife as 'rib' alludes to the Genesis story of Eve made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a social group of related families, a clan.

clue.text: Aspect of theatre in decline — scoundrel ain't upset

parts.note: a drop is a fall or decline
a cur is a contemptible man

indicators.note: upset tells us to tip over and rearrange the letters of the slang contraction

explanation.surface: Theatre is going downhill, and a villain overturns the word ain't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AINT to TAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop curtain is a stage cloth lowered between scenes, a feature of the theatre.

clue.text: When left, soldier's showing list

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a soldier is a caste of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier leaves and shows a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is a verb here, to lean or tilt as a ship does, not a register. A soldier ant is the caste that defends the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: To list is to lean over to one side, so slanting or tilted describes it.

clue.text: One dressed for athletics?

definitions.meaning: a single person or thing on its own
wearing a sleeveless running vest, a ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into SINGLET ON, an athlete's vest being worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lone individual or single card is a single item, while the split reading means wearing a running vest.

clue.text: Mean people left Hollywood area, upset with famous actors

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the whole run of pieces is turned upside down

parts.note: rats are mean, treacherous people
LA, Los Angeles, is the city that holds Hollywood

explanation.surface: Unkind people have left Hollywood, upset, taking big stars with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole of RATS L LA backwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A film with an all-star cast features many celebrated performers.

clue.text: Magnate's year with company brought in a good deal

indicators.note: brought in means these letters are placed inside the large-amount word

parts.note: tons, a ton, means a lot or a good deal

explanation.surface: A businessman's year with his firm brought in plenty of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' signals the container; 'a good deal' is tons, a large amount, not a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy and powerful business leader.

clue.text: Heavy metal item novice dropped in tart

indicators.note: dropped in means the beginner word is placed into the pastry word

parts.note: a flan is an open pastry tart
a tiro is a beginner

explanation.surface: A rock music thing, with a beginner falling into a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests rock music, but the item is a literal heavy metal object; 'dropped in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat iron is a heavy metal smoothing iron heated on a stove, an old household item.

clue.text: Printer's space by bar reduced as a single unit

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of space

indicators.note: reduced means the bar word loses its last letter

parts.note: block can mean to bar or obstruct

explanation.surface: A typesetting gap beside a shortened bar, taken all together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the K from BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is French for all together, treated as one whole.

clue.text: Take up is limited by ebbing attention

indicators.note: limited by means the word is is enclosed on both sides by the other letters
ebbing means going back, so the attention word runs backwards

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A pickup is restricted by fading attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' turns the attention word round to RAE, and 'limited by' signals that it encloses the clue's 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it, a synonym for taking it up.

clue.text: Artist, head of Academy, allowed to be cited in verse

indicators.note: to be cited in means these letters are quoted within the verse word

parts.note: a canto is a section of a long poem

indicators.note: head of means only the first letter of Academy is used

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A painter, the head of the Academy, is allowed a mention in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cited in' signals that the Academy's initial and the allowed word are quoted inside the verse word.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian painter of city views.

clue.text: "Sun' and "Terra 'not represented as' galactic object'?

indicators.note: represented as says the three words are reshaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Sun and Earth are not to be portrayed as a galactic body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented as' rearranges SUN TERRA NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron star is the collapsed core of a massive star, an object in a galaxy.

clue.text: Cleaner achievement — crowd to gather, though not at first

parts.note: a feat is an achievement
a herd is a crowd

indicators.note: not at first means the gather word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to muster is to gather

explanation.surface: A cleaner's achievement is drawing a crowd, though not at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' drops the M from MUSTER. The grid prints P for F; the wordplay builds the real word.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather duster is a tool of plumes on a stick used for cleaning.

clue.text: Cultivating men?

parts.note: read as the business of tending married men, as if spouses were a crop

explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as HUSBAND plus -RY, as though it were the farming of spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is farming, the cultivation of crops and animals.

clue.text: Love: charge for services involving one from Far East

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: involving means the charge word wraps round the letter for one

parts.note: a rental is a charge paid for the use of something
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Love: the fee for services includes one person from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts I inside RENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: The venue for a meal that is a moving experience

definitions.text: The venue for a meal that is a moving experience

parts.words: The venue for a meal that is a moving experience
parts.note: an eating place that is itself in motion, on a train

explanation.walkthrough: 'moving experience' sounds emotional but means literally travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining carriage on a train serves meals as the train moves.

clue.text: Dissemination part curtailed by ruffian

indicators.note: curtailed means the part word has its tail cut off

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
a lout is a rough, uncouth man

explanation.surface: A role was cut short by a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the E from ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the launch or spread of a new product to the public.

clue.text: Particular church right to get volunteers in

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A specific church is allowed to bring in volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain, as in 'a certain person', means specific or particular.

clue.text: Writing found in southern tomb, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the tomb word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a crypt is an underground burial vault

explanation.surface: Writing found in a tomb in the south, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' swaps CRYPT for its sound-alike spelling CRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is a text or handwriting, a piece of writing.

clue.text: Vegetarian side-dish: company line having no name on tin

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so no name follows the tin

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A meat-free side dish: a firm's product line with no name on the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Colcannon is an Irish dish of mashed potato with cabbage or kale.
explanation.definitionFit: Colcannon is a meatless Irish accompaniment of potato and greens.

clue.text: Eat ravenously-it's good tucking into bloody stuff

indicators.note: tucking into means the good letter goes inside the blood word

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

explanation.surface: Gobbling food, with the good tucking into something bloody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself greedily with food.

clue.text: Automaton's energy linked to lunar vehicle

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions

explanation.surface: A robot's power source is attached to a moon buggy.
explanation.walkthrough: A golem is the clay figure of Jewish folklore brought to life.
explanation.definitionFit: A golem is an animated humanlike figure, so a robot or mindless automaton.

clue.text: Opera heroine is mostly from history

indicators.note: mostly means the history word loses its last letter

parts.note: olden means from times past

explanation.surface: An operatic heroine is largely drawn from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the N from OLDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: Firm nets knocked over with incursion of the Atlantic initially

indicators.note: with incursion of means letters break into the reversed nets word
knocked over means the nets word is turned back to front

parts.note: trawls are large fishing nets

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Sturdy nets are overturned when the Atlantic first breaks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns the nets word round to SLWART, and 'with incursion of' puts the initials of 'the Atlantic' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means sturdy and steadfast, a synonym for firm.

clue.text: Sea-nymph, testy at sea, ensnaring hearts

indicators.note: ensnaring means the jumbled letters trap the hearts letter
at sea means confused, so the letters of the irritable word are jumbled

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: An irritable sea-nymph out on the waves traps hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges TESTY to TETYS, and 'ensnaring' puts H inside it. Tethys was a Titan goddess of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethys is a sea goddess of Greek myth, a daughter of Uranus and Gaia.

clue.text: Villain has edge in infiltrating US state

indicators.note: infiltrating means these letters slip inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A villain has the advantage when infiltrating an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has edge' suggests an advantage; it is the rim, and 'infiltrating' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal is a lawbreaker, a villain.
